mechanism: Both drugs have anticholinergic properties and CNS depressant effects; primidone induces CYP450 metabolism while scopolamine undergoes hepatic metabolism, and additive anticholinergic/sedative effects increase risk of cognitive impairment and reduced seizure control.
action: Monitor for increased sedation, anticholinergic symptoms, and seizure breakthrough; consider alternative antimuscarinic agent if scopolamine is necessary; assess seizure control regularly.
